messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SLO breach detected: cont-batch path p99 increased to 1.8s (SLO 1.0s) across us-west-2. Alerts triggered for streaming and gen routes. Paging eng-oncall.
oncall-elena: on it. seeing p95 ~480ms, p99 ~1.8s, error rates unchanged. Streaming stalls and long tail on cont-batch worker pods. moving to triage.
sre-eli: same. noticed queue length for packer queue spiking on a subset of nodes (nodepool-usw2-x). KV cache evictions spiked ~40% in last 5m.
runtime-kate: hypothesis: mixed sequence-length requests are creating oversized batches that delay short requests. packing code shows a few very large batches that block streaming workers.
eng-ryan: can we force max_batch_size lower as quick mitigation? what knobs do we have?
infra-jo: we can roll a config patch to the batcher via redwoodctl. quick command:

```
redwoodctl set batcher.max_batch_size=8 --scope=us-west-2
redwoodctl set batcher.mixed_seq_threshold=0.6 --scope=us-west-2
```

these are safe config flips, no deployment needed.
oncall-elena: good, do it. also enable preemptive_shedding for streaming routes so a long batch can be split earlier.

```
redwoodctl set batcher.preemptive_shedding=true --route=streaming
```

support-aliya: if we throttle batch size, latency for heavy requests will likely rise but short requests should recover. heads up: a high-value customer (acme-ai) reported degraded interactive responses ~5m ago.
prod-jess: tagging acme-ai as potential impacted. @cust-success-mike can you coordinate a short note? we may need to notify if breach continues >30m.
cust-success-mike: on it. drafting: "We're investigating higher latency on real-time features in us-west-2; engineering is mitigating. We'll update in 15 minutes." sending after confirmation.
sre-eli: rollback plan ready if config change introduces regression: revert batcher.max_batch_size to previous value and disable shedding. also we have a canary scope flag.
eng-ryan: quick check of logs: found repeated lines where packer waits >600ms for a batch to fill because a couple of massive-seq requests are pinned to same worker:

```
2026-03-15T18:02:33Z packer.cc: enqueue wait 612ms batch_id=0x7f seq_len=2048 route=streaming
2026-03-15T18:02:33Z packer.cc: enqueue wait 610ms batch_id=0x7f seq_len=2048 route=streaming
```

we should also consider moving large-seq requests to a dedicated pool or lower-priority class.
runtime-kate: agree. short-term: apply max_batch_size=8 and enable preemptive_shedding. mid-term: add classification to route seq_len>1024 to a "large-seq" pool.
oncall-elena: infra-jo executing the commands now.
infra-jo: applied max_batch_size=8 and preemptive_shedding=true in scope us-west-2. confirming flags:

```
redwoodctl get batcher --scope=us-west-2
# shows max_batch_size=8 preemptive_shedding=true mixed_seq_threshold=0.6
```

monitoring.
incident-bot: Update: p99 down to 1.2s 2m after change, p95 420ms. still above target.
sre-eli: good trend. initiating ephemeral routing: move streaming traffic to fallback model variant with faster KV access for 10% of traffic to relieve pressure.
eng-ryan: running rollout via router policy:

```
redwoodctl set routing.rule streaming fallback_variant=fast-kv weight=10% --scope=us-west-2
```

will monitor.
support-aliya: acme-ai notified (initial message sent). alerted account team.
cust-success-mike: they replied: "seeing improvements but still occasional stalls" - will share updates.
incident-bot: p99 now 0.9s after traffic shift. SLO under target for 1m.
oncall-elena: keep monitoring for 15m. assign owners: runtime-kate and eng-ryan to draft long-term plan (large-seq pool + batching heuristics). sre-eli owns rollback/runbook and monitoring thresholds. infra-jo stay on config changes. support-aliya and cust-success-mike handle customer comms. prod-jess to own postmortem if needed.
runtime-kate: logging followups: we need counters for batch wait time, per-node packer queue depth, and per-route seq_len distribution. I'll open an eval dashboard ticket.
eng-ryan: created quick dashboard pinned to oncall channel.
prod-jess: thanks all. if this holds we can close incident after 30m stable. moving to watch state. :thumbsup:
oncall-elena: handing off to night oncall in 30m — next oncall @sre-eli will monitor. leaving notes: changes made, observed p99 improvement, customer notified. please escalate if p99 >1.0s again.
sre-eli: acknowledged, will keep 1:1 paging for any regression. will follow up with root cause analysis and link to postmortem.
